levels.name: Diagnostic Integrity
levels.purpose: Validate the diagnostics frame before trusting its output.

levels.name: Target Context
levels.purpose: Resolve target, runtime context, VCS state, paths and basic executability.

levels.name: Repository Inventory
levels.purpose: Collect bounded technology-neutral evidence about repository shape and capabilities.

levels.name: Repository Hygiene
levels.purpose: Detect repository-level integrity and hygiene hazards.

levels.name: Tooling Discovery
levels.purpose: Discover project manifests, automation surfaces and candidate tools without making them mandatory.

levels.name: Declared Validations
levels.purpose: Execute only validations explicitly declared by the local diagnostics configuration.

levels.name: Security Hygiene
levels.purpose: Perform bounded conservative hygiene checks without claiming a security audit.

levels.name: Architecture Lock
levels.purpose: Verify the v1 architecture locks, canonical src tree, required schemas/source contracts, and absence of competing application/grammar trees.

levels.name: Python Architecture Integrity
levels.purpose: Parse active Python sources, resolve src-layout imports, enforce hexagonal dependency direction, confine PGF to the adapter, and reject per-language core branching.

levels.name: Contract & Schema Integrity
levels.purpose: Validate the eleven public/runtime schemas, canonical examples, unique schema identities, and documentation-manifest alignment.

levels.name: RuntimeSet & Capability Model
levels.purpose: Inspect composed immutable RuntimeSets, pinned artifact hashes, capability manifests and public release validation when runtime artifacts are deployed.

levels.name: SA↔GF Contract
levels.purpose: Validate the executable SA↔GF v1 operation registry, strict bridge consumption contract, and PGF-binding readiness without compiling grammar sources.

levels.name: Faithfulness & Planning Invariants
levels.purpose: Probe semantic→communication→language planning, obligation/semantic-reference coverage, and fail-closed no-fallback invariants without requiring a language RuntimeSet.

levels.name: Public SDK / CLI / HTTP Surface
levels.purpose: Import the canonical package and verify the public Python SDK, CLI commands, and minimal HTTP route surface without starting a server.

levels.name: Canonical Validation & Conformance
levels.purpose: Execute the target repository's canonical validator and state whether a real language RuntimeSet participated in release-grade validation.

levels.name: Adversarial Semantic Invariants
levels.purpose: Attack validation, obligations, coverage, deadlines, polarity and canonical operation selection with deterministic negative probes.

levels.name: RuntimeSet Mutation & Release Integrity
levels.purpose: Build synthetic immutable RuntimeSets outside the target checkout and verify fail-closed behavior under artifact, capability, evidence, activation and version mutations.

levels.name: Bridge & Lexical Adversarial Contract
levels.purpose: Attack SA↔GF bridge slot/feature consumption, contract compatibility, concrete-language resolution and exact lexical binding without a real PGF.

levels.name: Determinism, Concurrency & Packaging Isolation
levels.purpose: Repeat full renders sequentially and concurrently, then build/install/import a wheel from a temporary source copy without mutating the target checkout.

semantik.description: SemantiK Architect v1 architecture, contracts, runtime model, faithfulness and public-surface validation without executing the full pytest suite.

standard.description: Primary SemantiK Architect v1 diagnostic campaign. Adds the target repository canonical validator/conformance test suite.

deep.description: Adversarial SemantiK Architect campaign: standard validation plus declared validators, semantic negative tests, RuntimeSet mutation, bridge/lexical attacks, determinism/concurrency and isolated packaging.
